He's also been consistently calling it out on FOMO\\n\\nBased on the wallet data I've received, he's currently holding around 1.1B BOOMER, representing approximately 1.6% of the total supply\\n\\nHis position was valued at roughly $49K when checked, with an estimated reference entry around $1.46M market cap and reported gains of over 100%\\n\\nThe data also shows several purchases on October 18, at market caps ranging from approximately $1.1M to $2.17M\\n\\nHowever, around 68.6% of the tokens in his position reportedly came from an external wallet, so I can't confirm his actual cost basis for the entire bag\\n\\nStill, he's clearly holding a meaningful amount of BOOMER\\n\\nI see this as a double-edged sword\\n\\nOn one hand, having a large KOL with skin in the game who keeps talking about the project can attract more traders, especially while the Robinhood Chain memecoin community is still developing\\n\\nOn the other hand, he's already sitting on substantial reported profits. If he starts taking profits, even selling part of his position could create significant psychological pressure on people who followed his calls\\n\\nAnd when a narrative becomes too dependent on one KOL, attention can disappear pretty quickly if that person moves on to another token\\n\\nI wouldn't buy $BOOMER just because Solstice is holding it, but his wallet is definitely one worth tracking\\n\\n5. Upcoming catalysts\\n\\nRight now, the most interesting potential catalyst revolves around Flywheel\\n\\nSolstice has recently been talking about a $100K buyback plan for this week, suggesting that $BOOMER could receive a significant share of that buying pressure, potentially around $50K\\n\\nIf buybacks actually happen at that scale, they could be meaningful relative to $BOOMER's current market cap\\n\\nBut I want to make one thing clear: the $50K figure for $BOOMER is currently a promoted expectation, not a confirmed amount already spent on buybacks\\n\\nThere are also several other things I'm watching :\\n\\n> Flywheel attracting more trading volume and new token launches\\n> Holder Rewards providing an additional incentive to hold\\n> Solstice continuing to promote the token on X and FOMO\\n> Other KOLs starting to pay attention to the Flywheel narrative\\n> Liquidity rotating back into Robinhood Chain memecoins\\n\\nIn my opinion, $BOOMER needs more than a few rounds of shilling to sustain a longer-term move\\n\\nThe most important question is whether Flywheel can generate consistent trading volume and maintain real buyback activity\\n\\n6. Holder Distribution & Market Structure\\n\\nBased on the data I have, $BOOMER currently has around 2,900 holders, with the top 10 holders excluding the liquidity pool controlling approximately 15% of the supply\\n\\nThat's not an unusually high concentration for a relatively new memecoin, but I'd still want to investigate connected wallet clusters before drawing conclusions about how decentralized the supply really is \\n\\nThe project also completed an airdrop migration from its old contract to the new one at a ratio of 0.75:1 \\n\\nThis may have helped retain some of its original holder base, although potential selling pressure from airdrop recipients is something to keep in mind\\n\\nLooking at the chart, $BOOMER previously reached an ATH near $4.2M market cap, while the latest 1H chart I checked showed it trading around $3M\\n\\nOne thing I find relatively encouraging is that after its initial rally, the token hasn't completely collapsed. Instead, it has mostly been consolidating within a fairly wide range\\n\\nHowever, volume has declined significantly compared to the launch period\\n\\nBecause of that, I wouldn't call the current structure a confirmed breakout just yet\\n\\n7. My personal trading plan\\n\\nAt the current market cap of around $3M, I'm not particularly interested in FOMO\\n\\nThe $3.3M–$3.5M area is the nearest resistance zone. If price manages to break above it with convincing volume, I'll watch for a potential retest of the previous ATH around $4.2M\\n\\nIf we get another pullback, these are the areas I'm watching :\\n\\n$2.3M–$2.5M MC : My first dip zone of interest. Price has previously shown some decent reactions around this area\\n\\n$1.8M–$2M MC : A deeper support area. If price returns here, I'll check volume, holder activity, and buybacks before considering an entry\\n\\nIf $BOOMER loses $1.8M without buyers stepping back in, I'd become much more cautious\\n\\nA move below $1.2M could indicate that the previous bullish structure has weakened significantly\\n\\nThese are simply areas I'm watching based on the chart, not guaranteed support levels\\n\\n8. Final thoughts\\n\\nPersonally, I think $BOOMER has a few interesting characteristics compared to many other memecoins on Robinhood Chain\\n\\nThe narrative is easy to understand, the SPY pairing fits the tokenized stocks theme, and Flywheel adds reward and buyback mechanisms with some reported activity behind them\\n\\nSolstice continuously calling the token on X and FOMO is also helping it stay on people's radar\\n\\nBut it's important to remember that $BOOMER is still a high-risk memecoin, without strong independent utility to support its long-term value\\n\\nHolder rewards don't automatically make a token go up. Buybacks don't guarantee price appreciation either, especially if selling pressure exceeds the buying demand\\n\\nFor now, I'm slightly bullish in the short term, mainly because the Flywheel narrative is still getting attention and the chart hasn't completely lost its consolidation structure\\n\\nThat said, I'm not buying simply because Solstice is holding or because people are talking about a $100K buyback\\n\\nI'd rather see trading volume return, actual buyback transactions confirmed, and continued growth in the holder base\\n\\nFor me, $BOOMER is worth keeping on the watchlist rather than chasing at the current
